Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

version noun

one person’s account of what happened

also version of events, his version, her version, the story goes

classical

Cic. de Or. 2.80: ut vērī similis narrātiō sit (Lewis & Short)

narrātiō, narrātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

an account, a narrative

Other words

  • fāma, fāmae f. — the story as people tell it

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Liv. 1.1.6: duplex inde fāma est; Liv. 29.21.1

    duplex fāma est, there are two versions of the story.

Examples

  • duplex inde fāma est: aliī proeliō victum Latīnum pācem cum Aenēā, deinde affīnitātem jūnxisse trādunt

    from here there are two versions: some say that Latinus, beaten in battle, made peace with Aeneas and then an alliance by marriageLiv. 1.1.6

See also version, tell a story, according to.
